nodes.label: Cloud Build Run Log (failed deploy, 2026-07-15)
nodes.rationale: Records a FAILURE status build where the 'gcloud run deploy --no-allow-unauthenticated' step exited with code 1, evidencing the authenticated-Cloud-Run-deploy requirement from PRODUCTION_CHECKLIST.md being enforced by the pipeline.

nodes.label: Google OAuth Integration
nodes.rationale: OAuth state consumption was made atomic (single read-and-delete operation) to close a replay/race window where state could be reused across concurrent flows; the Google userinfo bearer token was moved from a URL query parameter to the Authorization header to stop token leakage via logs/referrers.

nodes.label: Google Secret Manager
nodes.rationale: Secrets (jwt-secret, session-secret, encryption-key, google-client-secret, mcp-api-key, database-url) are stored in Secret Manager rather than hardcoded so they can be rotated by adding new versions and redeploying, with a documented 90-day rotation cadence and fail-fast production validation of secret presence/length.

nodes.label: PKCE S256 Verifier Mechanism
nodes.rationale: PKCE with S256 and a high-entropy verifier was chosen over plain PKCE/no-PKCE so the OAuth authorization code exchange cannot be hijacked by an attacker who intercepts the code.

nodes.label: CSRF Same-Site Origin Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Origin/referer presence is now required and checked for unsafe HTTP methods in production/staging (via requireSameSiteOrigin) because cookie-based auth is otherwise vulnerable to cross-site request forgery when origin metadata is missing.

nodes.label: MCP API Key Authentication (constant-time)
nodes.rationale: MCP API key comparison uses timingSafeEqual plus explicit length checks instead of direct string comparison, eliminating a timing side-channel that could let an attacker infer the correct key byte-by-byte.

nodes.label: JWT Verification (algorithm/issuer/audience/claim checks)
nodes.rationale: JWT verification enforces algorithm/issuer/audience and re-validates decoded claim types (sub, email) after verify, and issuance now includes a jti, because trusting decoded claims implicitly or omitting a token id weakens revocation/audit and opens algorithm-confusion style risks.

nodes.label: CORS Explicit Allowlist Policy
nodes.rationale: ALLOWED_ORIGINS is an explicit comma-separated allowlist with wildcard origins always ignored, and localhost is only auto-allowed in development, so that browser-facing endpoints cannot be reached from arbitrary or wildcard origins in production.
